label: wherewhen - Data Restore
info:
PLAN.md §20 — reads a backup produced by wherewhen_data_export_flow.json and rewrites InfluxDB from it. Manual trigger ONLY, deliberately — explicitly for the wipe/migrate scenario (a freshly bootstrapped InfluxDB, new org/bucket/token per INFLUXDB_V2_SETUP.md), not for restoring into an instance that still has the old data. Edit the trigger's payload (backup_dir) before clicking, same pattern as oura_backfill_flow.json's manual trigger.

GoDaddy-side restore is NOT reinvented here — that stays import.php reading the existing disaster-recovery JSON archive (PLAN.md §4), which already works. This flow is strictly the InfluxDB-only half.

THE RISKIEST PART OF THIS FLOW, flagged per PLAN.md §20's own caution that this is 'the highest-stakes flow in the project': reconstructing InfluxDB line-protocol from the annotated CSV InfluxDB's query API produces (n_wdr_parse_csv_to_lines). Handles multiple table/header blocks in one CSV response (Flux groups different tag-combinations of the same measurement into separate annotated blocks) by re-detecting a new header row whenever one appears, rather than assuming exactly one header block per file — REASONED FROM DOCUMENTED FLUX CSV FORMAT, NOT CONFIRMED against a real multi-table export. Writes one field per line-protocol point rather than combining a series' multiple fields into one line — relies on InfluxDB's own documented behavior of merging same-measurement/same-tags/same-timestamp writes at the storage layer, not on this flow doing that merging itself.

Simplification, not full robustness: restores each measurement file in ONE write POST, not chunked like oura_backfill_flow.json's 500-line batches — acceptable for a rare, human-supervised operation, but flag if a real run ever hits a body-size error on a very large measurement.

Verify mode (§20's 'still open' item, resolved here): after restoring, runs a Flux count() per measurement and compares against the export manifest's row_count — a BALLPARK sanity check (the manifest's row_count includes CSV header/annotation lines, so exact equality isn't expected), not a byte-exact guarantee.

UNTESTED — never run against a live InfluxDB instance, and this flow's core logic could not be verified against real Flux CSV output during development. Companion test flow (wherewhen_data_restore_test.json) checks the CSV parser against a hand-built fixture matching the documented format, but that is not the same as a real InfluxDB response — treat this flow with real caution on first use, per its own tab info.

name: Manual trigger — EDIT payload before clicking
Capture backup_dir
Load secrets + start job log
Set manifest filename
func: return { payload: flow.get('wdr_backup_dir') + '/manifest.json', secrets: flow.get('wdr_secrets'), job_started_at: flow.get('wdr_job_started_at') };

name: Parse manifest, list CSVs
Parse file list (empty = nothing to restore)
Split: one message per CSV file (manual fan-out, Aug 2026 split-node fix)
Parse annotated CSV -> InfluxDB line protocol
InfluxDB: write restored lines (one POST per file — see tab info)
Join: wait for all file restores
comment: Paired with n_wdr_split_files via msg.parts (mode: auto).

name: Prep verify pass (list of measurements to count)
Split: one message per measurement to verify (manual fan-out, Aug 2026 split-node fix)
Build count() Flux query for this measurement
Extract count from CSV response
Join: wait for all verify counts
comment: Paired with n_wdr_split_verify via msg.parts (mode: auto).

name: Build verify report (ballpark, not exact)
Log success + update HA status
Prepare finish-point write
Catch any flow error (job_failed gap, Aug 2026)
comment: Fixes the gap flagged in PLAN.md §20's 'Known gap' note — this flow previously only handled its success path. Nothing in this flow has a native error output, so a catch node is what actually detects a real failure (a missing/corrupt manifest, a bad CSV parse, an InfluxDB write error). Scope null = catches any node on this tab. Given this is the highest-stakes flow in the project (§20's own framing), a caught failure here matters more than anywhere else — it means a restore didn't fully succeed and needs a human look, not silent trust.

name: Log failure + update HA status
SQLite: ensure job_status table exists
sqlite: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
SQLite: prep status UPSERT
